messages:
alex: Heads up — noticed a drift between control-plane reported canary split and actual routing on a couple of private VPC installs. Console shows 15% canary but telemetry and ingress logs show 0% on those nodes. :thinking:
maria: Which clusters are affected? private-only or hybrid?
alex: private-eu-2 and private-us-west-3, both air-gapped (signed-bundle flow). route_e2e_mismatch_count spiking for some customers behind those clusters.
cheng: Could be bundle propagation or agent-side manifest validation. We had a checksum edge-case in the v2 manifest logic last month. Any agent logs?
alex: Agent logs report: "manifest-checksum mismatch, skipping apply". Control plane logs show apply successful, so CP thinks it's live but nodes ignore.
sam: That would explain console vs real traffic. CP increments an applied counter when it pushes config; nodes never actually join the split. We need node acks before the UI marks the rollout as applied.
maria: We already have an async ack API for private installs. Proposal: change rollout UX to surface an intermediate state like "pending node-acks" when ack coverage < threshold.
cheng: Implementation idea: rollout.policy.canary.require_node_ack boolean (default false). For private installs default true. When true, control plane waits (or gates auto-flip) until ack_rate >= configured percent.
alex: Also add metrics: controlplane_propagation_ms, node_ack_rate, and per-cluster ack coverage. Gate auto-flip when ack_rate < 90%.
deploy-bot: Canary policy applied to service payments-api: split=15%/85% (id: rb-rollout-1805551234)
maria: We need a reconciliation loop to detect nodes that never ack. In air-gapped flows the signed S3 URL can expire before a manual pull, causing nodes to skip.
cheng: Add a TTL refresh step: when manifest TTL < 1h, reissue signed URL and bump manifest version to force reattempt. Also surface checksum mismatches with explicit error codes.
sam: Short-term: show a console warning if CP reports applied but node_ack_coverage < 95% across target clusters. Tooltip text: "Some private clusters have not acknowledged this rollout. Console split may not reflect actual routing."
alex: Found a customer where firewall rules blocked the ack callback outbound. We should add a diagnostics tab listing failed ack reasons per cluster (checksum, network, expired-url, auth-failure).
maria: Release plan items: 1) enable require_node_ack default-on for Private, 2) add node_ack metrics and dashboard panels, 3) display pending/partial states in console, 4) implement TTL refresh for signed bundles.
cheng: Backend changes: add per-rollout ack state table in controlplane DB (rollout_id, cluster_id, ack_state, last_seen). Expose wait_for_node_ack boolean in /rollouts/create. Avoid changing hosted default.
sam: API debate: should wait_for_node_ack be implicit (via environment) or an explicit rollout flag? I suggest implicit default + explicit override allowed.
alex: UX: default on for Private, off for Hosted, with an override toggle in console and API. Console should show effective policy and offer a "force proceed" escape hatch with a strong warning for private installs.
maria: Tests: add e2e that simulates agent returning checksum mismatch and verify rollout remains in pending state and UI shows the warning.
cheng: Also add an SRE escape path: allow operators to force-apply in emergencies but require audit log and an additional confirmation step.
alex: I'll open a PR that adds node_ack metrics, extends the rollout API, and updates console states. Will include migration script for in-flight rollouts to populate ack table.
sam: Ping me on the PR, I can add the dashboard widgets and alerts.
deploy-bot: Follow-up issue created: RDW-1047 "private canary ack gating + diagnostics" — triage tomorrow. :calendar: 
julia: I'll write a short customer note explaining the new pending state and recommended firewall rules for agent callback endpoints.
alex: Immediate action: add a temporary alert for route_e2e_mismatch_count > 5 in 5m for private clusters so we detect regressions while rolling this out. :eyes:
